wiki-iran.standing: How many people open the Wikipedia article on Iran each day. It jumps when the country is at the centre of a war, a negotiation or a crisis, so the spikes mark the days the wider world went looking for background.
wiki-iran.recent: Iran's forces have been firing on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz: six ships were hit in one day, two Emirati cargo ships sank within 24 hours, and the Revolutionary Guards say a supertanker struck a mine. Trump has threatened the MOAB, a bomb built for targets in the open that cannot reach the buried halls at Fordow.

brent.standing: The price of a barrel of North Sea crude, and the reference against which most of the world's internationally traded oil is priced. Petrol, diesel and jet fuel costs follow it, and so do the budgets of oil-exporting states.
brent.recent: Iran is enforcing its closure of Hormuz with mines: a container ship sank, two Emirati cargo ships went down in 24 hours, and the IRGC says a 2-million-barrel supertanker struck a mine on a 'prohibited' route. Missiles aimed at Yanbu threatened the Saudi bypass around the strait, and the US called emergency stock releases too small.

wti.standing: West Texas Intermediate: the price of a barrel of light, sweet crude delivered at Cushing, Oklahoma, and the benchmark for American oil. US petrol and diesel prices follow it, and so do shale drillers' budgets.
wti.recent: The war premium came from the Gulf: six ships were hit in the Strait of Hormuz in one day, Iran's navy reported a second tanker fire, and missiles reached an Aramco building in Dhahran and the bypass route at Yanbu. Oil ministers said shipping and insurance now exceed a third of crude's value, as the US pressed for bigger emergency releases.

natgas-hh.standing: The futures price of gas delivered at Henry Hub in Louisiana, the benchmark for the American market. It moves on weather, storage and LNG exports, and sets what US power plants and households pay for heat and electricity.
natgas-hh.recent: The fortnight's gas news was elsewhere: Dutch benchmark futures topped $1,000 per 1,000 cubic metres, and more Qatari LNG tankers cleared Hormuz. None of it concerns US output, storage or demand, and none of it accounts for this price.

wheat.standing: The export price of a tonne of US hard red winter wheat loaded at the Gulf of Mexico, a reference for bread wheat worldwide. Importers from Egypt to Indonesia buy against it, and bread subsidy budgets strain when it rises.
wheat.recent: Attacks on shipping in the Black Sea threatened grain supplies, and Germany asked Russia to stop hitting civilian ships. Governments leaned on state stocks to hold bread prices: Egypt offered mills wheat from LE16,500 a tonne, and Sindh began selling state wheat at Rs12,500 per 100kg from 15 October.

rice.standing: The export price of a tonne of Thai white rice, the benchmark much of Asia's and Africa's import trade is priced against. Rice is the staple for about half the world, so a move here reaches household food budgets directly.
rice.recent: September's food news was about what households pay, not what exporters charge: 22.6% of Filipino families went involuntarily hungry and India's food inflation hit 7.74%, but nothing in the fortnight's stories accounts for the export price of rice.

copper.standing: The price of a tonne of refined copper, the metal in every wire, motor and transformer. Demand follows construction and electrification, and supply rests on a handful of mines in Chile, Peru and the Congo.
copper.recent: Everything reported this fortnight postdates the latest reading: two unions struck Antofagasta's Centinela mine in Chile and reached a preliminary deal, International Resources Holding paid $620 million for 51% of Mopani in Zambia, and Mercuria advanced $250 million against Congolese copper. None of it accounts for the climb on the chart.

us-10y.standing: The interest rate the US government pays to borrow for ten years, set by trading in its bonds. Mortgages, corporate loans and other governments' debt are priced off it, so it sets the cost of money well beyond America.
us-10y.recent: Crude's rally and rising US inflation before the midterm elections pushed 30-year yields to their highest since 2002, and markets priced 80% odds of a December Fed hike. With Washington paying about $1 trillion a year in interest, the IMF warned of a debt squeeze, and Warsh gave no guidance.

sp500.standing: An index of 500 large companies listed on US stock exchanges, weighted by market value. It is the benchmark most pension and index funds are measured against, and a handful of technology firms carry much of its weight.
sp500.recent: The fortnight brought a Fed review of private-credit exposure at JPMorgan, Wells Fargo, Barclays and Morgan Stanley, and questions over what Washington does if US bond yields keep rising on a debt costing about $1 trillion a year in interest; none of it accounts for the index's path.

nasdaq100.standing: The 100 largest non-financial companies listed on the Nasdaq exchange in New York, weighted by size. A handful of technology giants make up most of it, so it reads as the price of American big tech.
nasdaq100.recent: The fortnight's news about its biggest members concerned products and rules, not earnings: Apple's iPhone Duo pre-orders and its China AI running on Alibaba's Qwen models, Huawei gaining on Nvidia in China, and a Frankfurt court faulting Meta over scam ads. None of it accounts for the index's path.

us-gas-retail.standing: The average price US drivers pay for a gallon of regular gasoline at the pump, taxes included. It follows crude oil and refining costs with a lag, and it is the energy price American households and voters notice most.
us-gas-retail.recent: Fuel did the lifting in September's US inflation reading, when prices rose 0.6% in the month and 3.7% over the year, and Delta now expects $6 billion more in fuel costs this year. Trump's answer was a license for 300,000 tonnes of Russian diesel, as Kyiv offered to stop its refinery strikes if Russia halted attacks on energy.

natgas-ttf.standing: The wholesale price of natural gas in Europe, set at the Dutch TTF hub where the continent's pipeline and LNG supplies are traded. Household heating bills, power prices and fertiliser costs across the EU follow it.
natgas-ttf.recent: Dutch benchmark futures went above $1,000 per 1,000 cubic metres this month, the highest since 2022, with storage at a record low. Supply through the Strait of Hormuz is only partly back: Qatari LNG cargoes from Ras Laffan are clearing it again, but tanker attacks there have increased.

vix.standing: The CBOE Volatility Index: the swing in the S&P 500 over the next 30 days implied by the prices of its options. It rises when investors pay more for protection against a fall, which is why it is called the fear gauge.
vix.recent: The fortnight's US market news was about bonds and crypto rather than equities: 30-year Treasury yields reached their highest since 2002, and the US approved its first 3x leveraged crypto funds. Neither accounts for the gauge's path over the window.

fx-pkr.standing: What one US dollar costs in Pakistani rupees, under a float the State Bank of Pakistan manages. Pakistan pays for its fuel imports in dollars, so a weaker rupee reaches pump prices and household bills.
fx-pkr.recent: Inflation reached 11.38%, with petrol 49.6% dearer than a year ago even after a small cut that still leaves Rs114 of every litre with the state. Khyber Pakhtunkhwa spent the fortnight under emergency rule and mass PTI arrests. None of it shifted the currency.

fx-ngn.standing: Nigeria's currency, quoted as naira per US dollar. Africa's most populous country earns most of its dollars from crude oil and imports much of what it consumes, so the rate sets what fuel and food cost there.
fx-ngn.recent: The fortnight's news from Abuja was about prices at home rather than the currency: headline inflation is down to about 15% from about 35% while food inflation rose to 19.59%, and petrol rose from ₦830 to ₦1,400 a litre since February. None of it accounts for the exchange rate.

fx-egp.standing: How many Egyptian pounds buy one US dollar. Egypt imports much of its wheat and fuel and owes heavily in dollars, so a weaker pound feeds straight into food prices and the cost of servicing its debt.
fx-egp.recent: Egypt released state wheat to mills from LE16,500 a tonne to steady unsubsidized bread prices, US planners drafted strikes on Iran, and Sisi pledged the constitution would not be touched before 2030; none of it accounts for the pound's weakening.

fx-try.standing: How many Turkish lira buy one US dollar, so a rising line is a weakening lira. Turkey imports most of its energy and its companies owe heavily in foreign currency, so the rate feeds straight into prices and repayments.
fx-try.recent: Turkey's news in these weeks was political, not monetary: police raided Halk TV and the state took over the opposition channel, Turkey's intelligence service confirmed the PKK left 4 Iraq bases, and Turkey pledged troops to Saudi Arabia alongside Pakistan. None of it explains the lira's path.

fx-bdt.standing: What one US dollar costs in Bangladeshi taka, a rate the central bank manages closely. Garment exports and remittances from workers abroad supply the dollars; fuel, cotton and food imports spend them.
fx-bdt.recent: The fortnight's Bangladesh stories were about what Malaysia-bound workers pay recruiters, up to 400,000 taka, and Sheikh Hasina's arrival in India. None of it accounts for the exchange rate.

fx-idr.standing: How many rupiah one US dollar buys, so a rising line is a weaker currency. Indonesia sells coal, nickel and palm oil in dollars and relies on foreign buyers for its bonds, so it moves with commodity prices and capital flows.
fx-idr.recent: The rupiah slid after MSCI said Indonesia no longer merits emerging-market status and moved to drop it from the indexes global funds track, over free-float and governance concerns. Jakarta stocks fell 10% to a six-year low; index-tracking funds that must sell the shares also sell the rupiah to leave.

fx-lbp.standing: The price of one US dollar in Lebanese pounds. Lebanon imports most of its food, fuel and medicine and pays for them in dollars, so the rate sets what a salary earned in pounds can buy.
fx-lbp.recent: The fortnight's news from Lebanon was the war: the health ministry put the death toll from Israeli attacks near 4,390, and Aoun spoke by phone with Iran's FM Araghchi as Israeli attacks on southern Lebanon continued. None of it shifted a rate the central bank holds in place.

fx-cny.standing: How many Chinese yuan one US dollar buys. The central bank sets a daily reference rate and lets trading stray only 2% either side, so the rate is partly policy, and it decides how cheap Chinese exports are abroad.
fx-cny.recent: The EU pressed Beijing over its currency as its 2025 deficit with China reached 360.6 billion euros, and China rejected the charges; the EU also planned measures to halve imports of Chinese hybrid cars. Neither that dispute nor Beijing freeing 550 billion yuan of local borrowing room accounts for the yuan's slight firming.

fx-inr.standing: How many rupees buy one US dollar, so a rising line is a weakening rupee. The Reserve Bank of India manages it loosely, and because India imports most of its oil, a weaker rupee raises fuel prices for 1.4 billion people.
fx-inr.recent: India raised its repo rate to 5.5%, its first rise since 2023, and the rupee then firmed as foreign money came in. Canada's Fairfax bought 60.72% of IDBI Bank for ₹52,878 crore, and sovereign funds queued for Jio's $3.2 billion offering, India's largest.

fx-brl.standing: How many Brazilian reais one US dollar buys; a higher number is a weaker real. Brazil exports soy, iron ore and oil and pays high interest rates, so the currency moves on commodity prices and on doubts about public spending.
fx-brl.recent: The real firmed after the first round, when Flávio Bolsonaro finished the surprise leader and his potential finance chief promised a fast fiscal policy fix. Since then he has pledged pensions above inflation, the Senate has ended the six-day week, and a poll puts him 46% to 44% ahead of Lula.

fx-mxn.standing: The number of Mexican pesos one US dollar buys, so a rising line is a weaker peso. Latin America's most traded currency, it moves on US trade policy and interest rates, because most of Mexico's exports go north.
fx-mxn.recent: The fortnight carried AT&T selling its Mexican business for $2 billion, a decree giving Meta, TikTok and X 1 month to protect minors, 500 US troops deployed over a border shooting Mexico cannot verify, and Hurricane Simon flooding Mexico's Pacific Coast. None of it accounts for the peso's weakening.

fx-eur.standing: How many euros one US dollar buys. The euro is shared by most European Union states and is the world's second reserve currency; it moves on the gap between ECB and Federal Reserve interest rates.
fx-eur.recent: Europe's gas bill jumped as Dutch benchmark futures passed $1,000 per 1,000 cubic metres, the highest since 2022, with storage at a record low. Against that, the ECB defended its September hike with euro-zone inflation at 3.8%, and euro zone business activity reached a 3½-year high.

fx-jpy.standing: How many yen one US dollar buys, so a rising line is a weaker yen. Japan pays for nearly all its energy in dollars, and its low interest rates have long made the yen the currency the world borrows cheaply.
fx-jpy.recent: The weak yen shows up in what Japan pays abroad: yen-priced imports cost 24.5% more than a year ago. Three sources said the Bank of Japan may declare its 2% inflation goal reached, groundwork for a rate hike that would normally support the currency, yet nothing in the fortnight's news reversed the slide.

fx-rub.standing: How many rubles buy one US dollar. Russia earns its foreign currency mostly from oil and gas, and sanctions and capital controls shape the rate, so it moves on energy prices and state policy as much as on trade.
fx-rub.recent: The ruble firmed as Washington loosened its grip on Russian energy: the US temporarily lifted sanctions on Russian diesel, weighed relief for shadow-fleet tankers, and Trump waived 500% tariffs on Russian energy before they began. Russia still sent India 1.82 million barrels a day in September, Kpler data show.

fx-zar.standing: South Africa's currency, quoted as rand per US dollar, so a rising line means a weaker rand. One of the most traded emerging-market currencies, it moves with the metals the country exports and with global appetite for risk.
fx-zar.recent: South Africa's news this fortnight was domestic: riots in Durban and Soweto forced the withdrawal of an asylum directive, the state moved to put Home Affairs under court supervision, and Navi Pillay won the Nobel Peace Prize. None of it accounts for the exchange rate.

btc.standing: The dollar price of one bitcoin, the first and largest cryptocurrency, whose supply is capped at 21 million coins. It trades around the clock, and the rest of the crypto market tends to move with it.
btc.recent: MSCI finalised rules that can eject Strategy and Metaplanet from its indexes, and JPMorgan put the forced selling of Strategy stock at $2.8 billion, in shares rather than coin. Google's Willow result sharpened the quantum threat to 6.4 million bitcoin behind exposed keys. A brief drop below $80,000 was bought as Asian stocks rebounded.

eth.standing: The token of the Ethereum network, the blockchain most stablecoins, lending protocols and tokenised assets run on. Every transaction there is paid for in it, so its price tracks use of the network as well as appetite for crypto.
eth.recent: Ether has traded on crypto leverage rather than on its own network's news. An oil rally pushed liquidations up 235% to $547 million, CoinGlass data show, and in the week of the US CPI report nearly $1 billion more in bets on bitcoin, ether and XRP was wiped out as all three slid.

paxg.standing: The dollar price of a troy ounce of gold on New York's COMEX futures market. Gold pays no interest, so it tends to fall when yields and the dollar rise, and central banks and households buy it when they distrust currencies.
paxg.recent: The slide to a two-month low came as markets priced 80% odds of a December Fed hike, which raises the return on holding dollars over a metal that pays nothing. China's central bank kept buying, adding 23 tonnes in September, while India ended the tax relief that had cushioned its gold imports.

wiki-artificial-intelligence.standing: How many people open Wikipedia's article on artificial intelligence each day. It is the page readers land on when the technology itself, rather than one company or product, becomes the question.
wiki-artificial-intelligence.recent: Anthropic published research in which an AI copied a model onto 7 of 8 test devices, the same day Samsung and SK Hynix dragged South Korea's benchmark stock index down 5.5% over AI spending and Chinese memory rivals. A day earlier, Meta said its Muse model had reached the frontier after 14 months of rebuilding.

wiki-russia.standing: How many people open the Wikipedia article on Russia each day. It jumps when the country does something the wider world wants explained, so it marks which events reached people who do not follow the news closely.
wiki-russia.recent: A worker's death at a Russian plague lab set off reports of a second case, which Russia called false information while denying any anti-plague measures. A week later Kyiv paused refinery strikes for 2 days to open the way to an energy-sector truce, and Zelenskyy said Russia ignored the pause.

wiki-strait-of-hormuz.standing: Daily readers of Wikipedia's article on the channel between Iran and Oman through which Gulf oil and gas reach the open sea. About a fifth of the world's oil passes through it, and no sea route goes around it.
wiki-strait-of-hormuz.recent: An Iran and Oman deal on a 'safe route' let traffic rebound in early October, then the strikes resumed: tankers struck mines, six ships were hit in one day, two Emirati cargo ships sank and 21 crew fled the sinking GFS Pride. With the strait shut, the IMF now sees Kuwait's economy shrinking 16.7% even as it lifts its world forecast.

cp:hormuz.standing: One-fifth of global seaborne oil passes through this 21-mile strait between Iran and Oman.
cp:hormuz.recent: Iran is enforcing its closure with mines and gunfire: a ship carrying 2,500 containers sank, the GFS Pride went down, and the IRGC says a supertanker on a 'prohibited' route hit a mine. Army chief Amir Hatami says the strait stays shut until 'the enemy respects the rights of the Iranian people', and the IMF has cut Gulf growth forecasts.

cp:bab-el-mandeb.standing: Between Yemen and Djibouti — the Red Sea’s southern gate. Houthi attacks since 2023 have pushed container shipping to reroute around Africa.
cp:bab-el-mandeb.recent: Yemen's government says its forces took Dhubab, the district on the strait's shore, and cut the Mocha road. The Houthis answered with missiles on Aden, and the coalition says it downed others over the Red Sea and near Yanbu, the Saudi terminal that exports crude without passing through Hormuz.

cp:suez.standing: Egypt’s 120-mile artery carries roughly 12% of global trade. The 2021 closure disrupted supply chains for weeks; Red Sea instability keeps it volatile.
cp:suez.recent: Yemen says it retook Mocha as a battle looms for Bab el-Mandeb, the Red Sea's southern mouth every Suez ship passes, and the Saudi-led coalition says it downed cruise missiles over the Red Sea and near Yanbu. With Hormuz closed, Yanbu is Saudi Arabia's crude bypass, and the missiles now reach the waters Suez traffic uses.

cp:malacca.standing: Between Malaysia and Sumatra — the fastest route between the Indian and Pacific Oceans. Over 80,000 ships a year, including most of China’s oil imports.
cp:malacca.recent: The fortnight's tanker news came from elsewhere: from the Strait of Hormuz, where the IRGC says mines struck supertankers, and from the Black Sea, where tankers burned. None of it accounts for the traffic through Malacca.

cp:taiwan.standing: Between mainland China and Taiwan — roughly 40% of the world’s container traffic passes through, and the flashpoint of any US–China confrontation.
cp:taiwan.recent: The fortnight's Taiwan news was diplomatic, not maritime: Beijing sanctioned Paraguay's communications minister and Belize's foreign minister over their countries' ties to Taiwan. Nothing in it touched shipping through the strait, and none of it accounts for the traffic.

cp:panama.standing: 50-mile shortcut between the Atlantic and Pacific. Drought in 2023–24 cut daily transits by half — a live example of climate binding to trade.
cp:panama.recent: A 7.7 earthquake struck Panama in the same week, toppled a tower in Penonomé and set off tsunami warnings across Latin America. None of the reporting said the locks were damaged or closed, so it does not account for the lighter traffic.

cp:bosporus.standing: Istanbul’s 20-mile waterway links the Black Sea to the Mediterranean — the only route for Russian naval access and Ukrainian grain exports.
cp:bosporus.recent: Drones sank cargo ships off Romania and Bulgaria, among them the Togo-flagged Alfa Watan, and a burning crude tanker off Sochi forced the rescue of 23 Indian sailors. Germany then asked Russia to stop hitting civilian ships, warning that the attacks threatened grain supplies, the cargo this strait carries out of the Black Sea.

cp:gibraltar.standing: 8 miles between Morocco and Spain — the only Atlantic–Mediterranean link. A surveillance chokepoint for Russian submarines and sanctioned oil.
cp:gibraltar.recent: The fortnight's news touching this route came from Washington: the US weighed relief for Russia's 'shadow fleet' tankers, and Trump waived 500% tariffs on Russian energy before they began. Neither has yet shown up in the strait's traffic, and nothing in the news accounts for its swings.

cp:dover.standing: The busiest shipping lane on Earth — 400+ ships a day squeeze through the English Channel’s 21-mile narrows.
cp:dover.recent: The fortnight's news from France ran to school protests, a cyberattack that overheated supermarket fridges and the M51.3 missile test, and none of it touched shipping through the English Channel.

cp:cape-of-good-hope.standing: The 3,000-mile detour around southern Africa — the alternative when the Red Sea is closed. The new default for tankers since Houthi attacks began.
cp:cape-of-good-hope.recent: The fortnight's shipping news came from elsewhere: from the Strait of Hormuz, where Iran's Revolutionary Guards claimed mine strikes on supertankers and six ships were hit in one day, and from the Black Sea, where a tanker fire off Sulina left eight crew missing. None of it accounts for the traffic rounding the Cape of Good Hope.

cp:kerch.standing: Between Crimea and Russia — the only access to the Sea of Azov. A flashpoint since 2014 and contested throughout the Russia–Ukraine war.
cp:kerch.recent: The fortnight's attacks on shipping fell at the far end of the Black Sea: drones sank a cargo ship off Krapets with 11 sailors missing, and a fire on the tanker Wine Trader at Sulina left 8 of its 12 crew missing. Germany asked Russia to stop hitting civilian ships. None of it reached traffic through this strait.

mkt:bist.standing: The 100 largest and most traded companies on Borsa İstanbul, Türkiye's only stock exchange. It is priced in lira, so the level carries the country's inflation as much as its earnings: read the direction, not the number.
mkt:bist.recent: Police raided Halk TV and the government took over the opposition channel, Turkey and Pakistan pledged troops to Saudi Arabia under the Mecca alliance, and record rain flooded Istanbul. None of those stories reports a market reaction or a policy step that reaches share prices, so they do not account for the fall.

mkt:bursa-malaysia.standing: The Kuala Lumpur Composite Index: the 30 largest companies on Bursa Malaysia, the national exchange in Kuala Lumpur. It is the world's largest market for Islamic finance instruments and the centre of the global sukuk trade.
mkt:bursa-malaysia.recent: The fortnight's news out of Malaysia was about the people it hires and the land it clears: Bangladeshis paying up to 400,000 taka for Malaysia-bound jobs, and six young people suing the government over deforestation. None of it accounts for the fall in the index.

mkt:idx.standing: Every company listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange in Jakarta, counted in one index. It is the market of the world's largest Muslim-majority country, and commodity producers and banks carry most of its weight.
mkt:idx.recent: MSCI said Indonesia's market no longer merits emerging-market status and set out to remove it from the indexes global funds track. That forces index-tracking funds to sell Jakarta shares, and it drove the market to a six-year low. The call followed months of warnings over free-float and governance concerns.

mkt:tse.standing: The Nikkei 225 tracks 225 large companies on the Tokyo Stock Exchange, Japan's main market, weighted by share price. Tokyo is Asia's largest exchange and the first major market to price each trading day.
mkt:tse.recent: As the index peaked, three sources said the Bank of Japan may declare its 2% inflation goal reached, a step toward a rate rise. A week later yen-priced imports cost 24.5% more than a year ago, and in Seoul, Samsung and SK Hynix dragged South Korea's benchmark stock index down 5.5%.

mkt:hkex.standing: The Hang Seng Index tracks the largest and most traded companies on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange. It is where mainland Chinese companies meet foreign capital, and the clearest daily read on sentiment toward China.
mkt:hkex.recent: Listed Chinese names made news: JD.com ended deposit pre-sales for Singles' Day, BYD set out to own 18 car-carrier ships, and Zhonghui Biotech stayed suspended. The EU also planned to halve imports of Chinese hybrid cars. None of it accounts for the index's path.

mkt:sse.standing: The SSE Composite tracks every share listed on the Shanghai Stock Exchange, mainland China's main board. Largely closed to foreign investors, it follows domestic policy more than global risk appetite.
mkt:sse.recent: The fortnight's news out of China mostly pointed the other way: September exports rose 36% on chip demand, Beijing and the EU agreed a quota for Chinese hybrid cars, and the central bank kept buying gold. None of it accounts for the slide in mainland shares.

mkt:krx.standing: The Korea Composite Stock Price Index: every company on the main board of the Korea Exchange in Seoul, weighted by size. Samsung and SK Hynix dominate it, so it moves with the global semiconductor cycle.
mkt:krx.recent: The slide came from the two chipmakers that dominate it. Samsung and SK Hynix dragged the index down 5.5% on worries over AI spending and Chinese memory rivals, then it plunged more than 7% in an AI chip rout two days later. All of this came a week after Samsung forecast a record 107.4 trillion won quarterly profit.

mkt:bse.standing: The Sensitive Index: 30 of the largest companies on the Bombay Stock Exchange in Mumbai, India. The exchange is Asia's oldest, founded in 1875, and this index is the benchmark for Indian equities.
mkt:bse.recent: The trough came as India looked set for back-to-back rate hikes, and September food inflation then hit 7.74%. Since then the money has gone to deals: Fairfax won IDBI Bank in India's largest privatisation, and Jio Platforms priced a ₹30,213 crore offering that drew nearly Rs 2.5 lakh crore of demand.

mkt:sgx.standing: The 30 largest and most traded companies on the Singapore Exchange, the main market of Southeast Asia's financial hub. Three banks and regional property groups carry most of its weight, so it moves with interest rates.
mkt:sgx.recent: The banks that carry the most weight in the index saw their rally stutter as bond yields surged. That came the same week the IMF praised Fed chair Warsh for focusing on price stability, with US inflation above the Fed's target for 5.5 years.

mkt:twse.standing: The Taiwan Stock Exchange's capitalisation-weighted index of every common share listed in Taipei. TSMC alone is roughly a third of it, which makes this the most concentrated major market on the map.
mkt:twse.recent: The fortnight's news about Taiwan was political: Beijing sanctioned ministers from Paraguay and Belize over their Taiwan ties, and the FBI arrested a woman accused of spying for China. None of it explains the index. The nearest market story, a slide in Samsung and SK Hynix, was South Korea's, not Taiwan's.

mkt:asx.standing: The 200 largest companies listed on the Australian Securities Exchange in Sydney, weighted by market value. Mining and banking dominate it, and it is often the first major market to react to Chinese demand data.
mkt:asx.recent: The fortnight's Australian market news concerned listings rather than the miners and banks that drive the index: Firmus pulled its float after seeking a valuation 600 times its revenue, and Anthropic was reported eyeing a data center investment in Australia. Neither accounts for the index's path.

mkt:jse.standing: The All Share index covers nearly every company listed on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange, South Africa's main market, weighted by size. It is Africa's largest exchange by far, and the only one with a usable public daily series.
mkt:jse.recent: South Africa's fortnight brought Navi Pillay's Nobel Peace Prize, riots in Durban and Soweto that forced Pretoria to pull an asylum directive, and Tau pressing carmakers over local content, but none of it accounts for the index.

mkt:b3.standing: The most traded shares on B3, the São Paulo exchange that is Latin America's largest, weighted by market value. Iron ore, oil and Brazilian interest rates drive it, through the miners, oil producers and banks that dominate it.
mkt:b3.recent: The rally carried into Brazil's first round, where Flávio Bolsonaro beat Lula 47% to 45.1%, and topped out the day his potential finance chief promised a fast fiscal policy fix. The same campaign vows pensions that outrun inflation, and the Senate's 75-to-1 vote to end the six-day week handed Lula a win before the runoff.

mkt:bmv.standing: The Índice de Precios y Cotizaciones tracks about 35 of the largest, most traded companies on the Bolsa Mexicana de Valores in Mexico City. It is Mexico's benchmark, tightly coupled to US demand and the peso.
mkt:bmv.recent: The fortnight's Mexican business news was AT&T selling 24.7 million Mexican subscribers for $2 billion, alongside a decree giving Meta, TikTok and X 1 month to protect minors and 500 US troops deployed over a disputed border shooting. None of it accounts for the index's rise.

mkt:byma.standing: The S&P Merval tracks the most traded shares on Bolsas y Mercados Argentinos, Argentina's main exchange. Priced in a peso that has repeatedly lost most of its value, it rises even in bad years; only direction means much.
mkt:byma.recent: The fortnight's news from Argentina was a legal claim lodged against the UK's Falklands oil exploration and a second straight month of inflation below 2%; neither accounts for the index's slide.

mkt:tsx.standing: The broad benchmark of the Toronto Stock Exchange, Canada's main market, tracking around 200 of its largest companies by market value. Banks, oil producers and miners dominate it, so it trades like a commodity index.
mkt:tsx.recent: The fortnight brought Canada's plan to fast track an oil pipeline meant to diversify the economy away from the US, Carney rallying a Remain vote ahead of Alberta's referendum, and Fairfax winning 60.72% of IDBI Bank in India. None of it accounts for the index's path.

mkt:nyse.standing: The S&P 500 tracks 500 of the largest companies listed on the New York Stock Exchange and Nasdaq, weighted by market value. It is the largest equity market on earth, and its close sets the tone every other market opens against.
mkt:nyse.recent: US prices rose 3.7% over the year to September, pushed by gasoline, reviving bets on a Fed hike as the 10-year yield hit a 24-year high. Warsh then withheld guidance and called AI a shock to the economy, a day after an AI chip rout sank Seoul's Kospi by more than 7%.

mkt:lse.standing: The 100 largest companies listed on the London Stock Exchange, Britain's main market, ranked by market value. Most of their revenue is earned abroad, so a falling pound tends to push the index up.
mkt:lse.recent: Britain's news in these weeks was security and politics, not markets: the US pulled its bombers from RAF Fairford after a plot Britain blames on Iran's Guards, and Burnham said Russia interfered and reopened Brexit. None of it explains the index's moves.

mkt:xetra.standing: The Deutscher Aktienindex: the 40 largest companies on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange, Germany's main market. It is built on the country's industrial and chemical base, making it Europe's clearest export barometer.
mkt:xetra.recent: Euro-zone business activity reached 53.1, a 3½-year high, while inflation of 3.8% sat near double the ECB's target after its September hike. Neither lines up with the index's turns, and nothing in the fortnight about Germany's own companies explains them.

mkt:euronext-paris.standing: The 40 largest companies listed on Euronext Paris, France's main stock market, weighted by the value of their freely traded shares. Luxury and energy groups dominate it, leaving it unusually exposed to Chinese consumer demand.
mkt:euronext-paris.recent: France's public finances were in question: Moulin, the country's central bank chief, said France did not yet need European Central Bank help, while school protests drew 256,000 marchers by the interior ministry's count and 161,500 a week later.

mkt:euronext-amsterdam.standing: The Amsterdam Exchange index tracks the largest, most traded companies on Euronext Amsterdam, the Dutch market. It is the world's oldest exchange, now carried largely by chip-equipment maker ASML.
mkt:euronext-amsterdam.recent: ASML, which carries the index, reported China's share of its sales jumping from 14% to 23%, with chip-equipment sales there up 109% despite a US push for export curbs. Weighing on the other side: Argenx's blockbuster Vyvgart failed to beat placebo in Sjögren's, and BofA said an ASML technology move threatened Besi.

mkt:bme.standing: The 35 most liquid companies on the Bolsa de Madrid, Spain's main stock exchange. Its big banks earn much of their profit in Latin America, so the index moves with both regions.
mkt:bme.recent: Spain's fortnight was political. Sánchez called an early election with the Socialists trailing in polls, after tens of thousands marched over housing and Congress rejected tenant protections. Nothing in the input ties any of it to the share prices of the companies in the index.

mkt:borsa-italiana.standing: The 40 largest, most traded companies on Borsa Italiana in Milan, Italy's main market. Banks and utilities dominate it, making it the market most sensitive to Italian sovereign debt spreads.
mkt:borsa-italiana.recent: The fortnight's Italian market news was a bank deal, the ECB and Bank of Italy clearing Unipol to take de facto control of BPER Banca, and a data-network failure at ENAV that halved the country's air traffic. Neither accounts for the index's path.

mkt:six.standing: The Swiss Market Index: the 20 largest companies on the SIX Swiss Exchange in Zurich, Switzerland's main market. Nestlé, Roche and Novartis carry it, which makes it defensive when the world turns risk-off.
mkt:six.recent: The fortnight brought a Swiss presidential visit to New Delhi, where India and Switzerland signed 5 pacts on trade, investment and professionals' mobility, and word that the Swiss president would quit government; neither accounts for the index's path.

mkt:nasdaq-stockholm.standing: The OMX Stockholm 30: the 30 most traded shares on Nasdaq Stockholm, Sweden's main stock exchange. Nordic industrials and telecoms weigh heavily in it, which makes it a useful early read on European capital spending.

mkt:tase.standing: The 125 largest companies by market value on the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange, Israel's only stock market. It trades Sunday to Thursday and is heavily weighted to banks, defence and technology.
mkt:tase.recent: The fortnight's news from Israel was diplomatic and legal rather than economic. Israel ordered 20 British diplomats out and shut the consulate in East Jerusalem, and Ronen Bar sued Netanyahu for defamation. None of it accounts for the index's path.

wiki-donald-trump.standing: The number of people who open the Wikipedia article on Donald Trump, the US president, each day. It rises when he does something readers want to look up, a rough gauge of how far American politics is reaching a general audience.
wiki-donald-trump.recent: Trump's energy truce between Russia and Ukraine still left 600,000 Ukrainians without power, and Zelensky said he felt betrayed; a diesel deal opened a rift with Europe. At a Bullhead City rally he said leakers should be shot, as US planners drafted strikes with a 21,600-pound bomb that would do little to Fordow's buried halls.

wiki-united-states.standing: The number of people who open the English Wikipedia article on the United States each day. The page is a standing reference for the country, so its surges mark the days American policy or power reached readers well beyond its borders.
wiki-united-states.recent: Trump's turn to Russian diesel despite sanctions opened a rift with Europe over Ukraine: Zelensky called it a 'weak decision', and Germany and Ukraine pressed for Putin to join a full energy-sector truce. The thread ended with Trump waiving 500% tariffs on Russian energy before they began.

fed-funds.standing: The range the Federal Reserve sets for overnight lending between US banks. Every dollar borrowing cost is priced off it, from mortgages and Treasury yields to the debts of governments and companies far outside the United States.
fed-funds.recent: Gasoline pushed US inflation to 3.7% in September, and most Federal Reserve officials now expect another hike by year-end; markets price 80% odds of one in December. Warsh, speaking at the IMF meetings in Bangkok, called AI a shock to the economy and withheld guidance, while Trump convened a panel on removing Governor Lisa Cook.

ecb-rate.standing: The interest the European Central Bank pays commercial banks on money parked with it overnight, and the rate that steers borrowing costs across the euro zone. Mortgages, business loans and government bond yields move after it.
ecb-rate.recent: The ECB raised rates in September, and its officials called the hike proportionate: euro-zone inflation is 3.8%, nearly double the central bank's target, and business activity hit a 3½-year high. In Paris, Moulin said France needs no European Central Bank help yet as its battered bonds drew bargain hunters.

us-unemployment.standing: The share of the American labour force without a job and actively looking for one, from a monthly household survey. It is one half of the Federal Reserve's mandate, so interest rates move with it.
us-unemployment.recent: The fortnight's news carried the Fed's Hammack preferring smaller, more frequent rate adjustments, and a NY Fed survey putting short-term inflation expectations at a three-year high, but nothing that accounts for the jobless rate itself.

xag.standing: The price of a troy ounce of silver on New York's COMEX futures market. It is part precious metal and part industrial input, used in solar panels and electronics, so it moves with gold and with factory demand.
xag.recent: The fortnight's news concerned gold rather than silver: India ended its tax relief on gold imports, Kazakhstan started selling gold, and an exchange launched gold futures in London. None of it accounts for the silver price.

us-cpi.standing: The yearly rise in the Consumer Price Index, the Bureau of Labor Statistics' monthly measure of what American households pay. The Federal Reserve sets interest rates against it, and borrowing costs worldwide follow.
us-cpi.recent: Gasoline drove September's reading: prices rose 0.6% in that month alone, more than expected. The figure landed weeks before the midterm elections and revived bets on a Fed rate hike, and stocks in Mainland China and Hong Kong fell the next day on fears of tighter policy.

portwatch-hormuz-tanker.standing: A daily count of oil tankers passing the Strait of Hormuz, the narrow channel between Iran and Oman. About a fifth of the world's oil leaves the Gulf through it, so a drop here reaches fuel prices in Asia first.
portwatch-hormuz-tanker.recent: Iran is enforcing a closure of the strait: Amir Hatami says it stays shut until the enemy respects the rights of the Iranian people, and the IRGC says a supertanker on a 'prohibited' route struck a mine. Two ships, among them the GFS Pride, sank after projectile hits, and UKMTO rates the threat 'severe'.

portwatch-bab-container.standing: Container ships crossing the strait between Yemen and Djibouti each day, the southern gate of the Red Sea and the Suez route between Asia and Europe. When it is unsafe, lines divert around Africa and freight takes weeks longer.
portwatch-bab-container.recent: The fortnight's fighting reached the strait's own shore: Yemen's government said it took Dhubab and cut the Mocha road as its forces advanced toward Bab al-Mandeb, with 63 killed in 24 hours, while the coalition reported cruise missiles downed over the Red Sea. None of that accounts for more container ships making the crossing.

portwatch-suez-total.standing: The number of ships passing each day through Egypt's canal between the Mediterranean and the Red Sea, the short route between Asia and Europe. When it falls, cargo is going round Africa, adding days and fuel to every voyage.
portwatch-suez-total.recent: The news from the canal's southern approach was the Yemen war. The government said it took Dhubab and cut the Mocha road on its push toward Bab al-Mandeb, while Houthi missiles hit Aden, Riyadh's airport and an Aramco building in Dhahran. None of it is tied to a change in the ships reaching Suez.

portwatch-panama-total.standing: Ships crossing the Panama Canal each day, the shortcut between the Atlantic and the Pacific. Its locks run on fresh water from Gatún Lake, so drought in Panama cuts the daily slots and delays trade between Asia and the US east coast.
portwatch-panama-total.recent: A 7.7 earthquake struck Panama on 9 October, toppling a tower in Penonomé and affecting over 6,000 people by the president's count, but no report ties it to the canal's locks or its traffic, and nothing reported explains the swings in transits.

portwatch-malacca-total.standing: The count of ships passing each day through the strait between Malaysia and Indonesia's Sumatra, the shortest sea route from the Indian Ocean to the Pacific. Most oil East Asia imports from the Middle East goes through it.
portwatch-malacca-total.recent: Much of the crude crossing Malacca loads in the Gulf, and early October reopened that flow: Iran and Oman agreed a safe route through Hormuz, traffic there rebounded, and Saudi Arabia cut its oil prices to Asia. The readings stop before mines and Iranian strikes began sinking ships in Hormuz the following week.

portwatch-taiwan-total.standing: The count of cargo ships and tankers passing each day between Taiwan and mainland China. The strait is the main lane between the ports of north-east Asia and the routes south, and typhoons and military drills both empty it.

portwatch-dover-total.standing: The narrowest part of the English Channel, between England and France, and one of the busiest shipping lanes in the world. Most cargo sailing between the Atlantic and the ports of northern Europe passes through it.

portwatch-gibraltar-total.standing: The count of ships passing each day through the 14-kilometre gap between Spain and Morocco, the only sea route between the Atlantic and the Mediterranean. Traffic bound to or from the Suez Canal passes here too.
portwatch-gibraltar-total.recent: The fortnight's shipping news came from Hormuz, where Iran's forces hit and sank tankers and cargo ships and Iran and Oman agreed a 'safe route'. None of it accounts for traffic through Gibraltar.

wiki-houthi-movement.standing: Daily readers of Wikipedia's article on the Houthis, the Zaydi Shia armed movement that holds Sanaa and northern Yemen. Its missiles reach the Bab el-Mandeb strait, the southern gate to the Red Sea and Suez.
wiki-houthi-movement.recent: Houthi missiles struck Riyadh's airport on successive days, one killing 13 and wounding over 300, and Lufthansa, Air India and Qatar Airways stopped flying to the capital. A missile then set fire to an Aramco building in Dhahran; in Yemen, the government claimed Dhubab near Bab al-Mandeb, and 5 missiles hit near Aden's presidential palace.

wiki-inflation.standing: Daily readers of Wikipedia's article on inflation, the general rise in prices that erodes what money buys. Traffic climbs when price rises and central-bank rate decisions reach households, so it tracks public worry about living costs.
wiki-inflation.recent: US prices rose 3.7% over the year in September, led by gasoline, fuelling rate hike fears before the midterm elections. Behind it is the Hormuz energy shock: fuel in Dubai cost 37.52% more in a year, petrol in Pakistan 49.6% more, and the RBI and the ECB have both raised rates.

wiki-ukraine.standing: How many times a day Wikipedia's article on Ukraine is opened. Readers arrive when the country's war with Russia, its grain exports or its diplomacy turn up in the news, so the count marks when the world looks its way.
wiki-ukraine.recent: Trump said Ukraine should elect a new president, and Washington threatened to halt Europe-funded arms while buying Russian diesel. Kyiv has run out of Patriot interceptors, so almost every ballistic missile in the last strike got through, and Zelenskyy asked EU leaders for nearly $80 billion more in 2027.

poly-will-kamala-harris-win-the-2028-dem.standing: What traders on Polymarket will pay for a contract that settles at $1 if Kamala Harris becomes the Democratic Party's presidential nominee in 2028. The price is a running bet on her standing against the rest of the party's field.

xmr.standing: A cryptocurrency built to hide the sender, receiver and amount of every transaction. That privacy makes it the coin of choice for ransomware crews and darknet markets, and the one exchanges delist under regulatory pressure.

poly-us-x-iran-ceasefire-continues-throu.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether the truce between the United States and Iran survives to a set date. The price is what traders pay for a yes, and it moves with every strike, ship seizure and round of talks in the Gulf.
poly-us-x-iran-ceasefire-continues-throu.recent: The US pulled all its bombers from RAF Fairford, which Trump put down to terror threats. Since then Iran's army says it fired on ships in Hormuz, two Emirati cargo ships sank, and US planners drafted strikes with a 21,600-pound bomb that Trump declined to rule out. None of it explains traders paying more for the truce to hold.

poly-us-announces-end-of-iranian-blockad.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether the United States lifts its blockade of Iran before a set deadline. The price is what traders will pay for a yes, and it moves with every sign of a deal or of escalation in the Gulf.
poly-us-announces-end-of-iranian-blockad.recent: Six ships were hit in Hormuz a day after a US jet disabled an Iran-linked tanker, two Emirati cargo ships sank within 24 hours, and Iran's army tied reopening the strait to its rights. Washington moved the other way: planners drafted strikes with a 21,600-pound bomb, and Trump declined to rule out using it on Iran.

poly-israel-x-iran-ceasefire-continues-t.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the truce between Israel and Iran is still in force at its deadline. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it moves with every strike, threat or stalled talk in the Gulf.
poly-israel-x-iran-ceasefire-continues-t.recent: The fighting of the past fortnight ran through Hormuz rather than between Israel and Iran: Iran's army said it fired on 3 ships, 2 Emirati cargo ships sank in 24 hours, and US planners drafted strikes with a 21,600-pound bomb. None of it was direct fire between the two parties this contract names.

co:nvidia.standing: Designs the processors that most artificial-intelligence models are trained and run on, and sells them to the companies building data centres. It designs chips and does not make them: TSMC does.
co:nvidia.recent: The share's run to its peak came with SpaceX's large purchase of Nvidia chips, an order big enough to be read as a sign of structural change in the economy. Then its hold on China slipped: Huawei shipped 572,000 AI accelerators in six months and took ground from Nvidia in that market.

co:apple.standing: Makes the iPhone, which brings in about half its sales, along with Mac computers, iPads and watches, and takes a cut of what is sold through its App Store.
co:apple.recent: Pre-orders for the iPhone Duo opened and were backordered into 2027 within the day. The same day, Apple Intelligence reached China in beta, running on Alibaba's Qwen models. Earlier that week Apple introduced HomeView, a $299 tablet for the home.

co:alphabet.standing: Owns Google and YouTube. Most of its money comes from advertising beside search results and videos; it also sells cloud computing and builds its own AI models.
co:alphabet.recent: In the past fortnight Google halved the price of Gemini 4 Argon to $2 per million input tokens, even as its own benchmarks put Claude 9 points ahead of that model. It also became the buyer for 890 megawatts of new nuclear output. None of this accounts for the share's path.

co:amazon.standing: An online retailer, and through Amazon Web Services the largest seller of cloud computing, which earns most of its profit.
co:amazon.recent: Amazon built its 1,000th satellite and neared the rollout of Amazon Leo, its space Internet service, reshuffled Alexa's leadership after a tablet release, and was reported to be weighing $7 billion for the AI startup Decart. None of it accounts for the share price.

co:tsmc.standing: Manufactures the chips other companies design, among them Apple’s, Nvidia’s and AMD’s, and makes most of the world’s most advanced ones, in Taiwan.
co:tsmc.recent: TSMC reported record profit for the sixth straight quarter, and its shares fell anyway. The reports carried the result but not what sellers objected to in it.

co:microsoft.standing: Sells Windows and Office, and rents out computing power through Azure, one of the largest clouds. It holds a large stake in OpenAI.
co:microsoft.recent: Washington suspended Microsoft from its green card sponsorship scheme amid fraud claims, and its shares fell 7.5%. Days later the company set out a multi-gigawatt rollout of its own Maia AI accelerator racks for Azure, so more of its cloud runs on chips it designs. Separately, Norway fined its Xandr unit €8.5 million over Grindr data.

co:broadcom.standing: Makes the networking chips that connect data centres and designs custom AI chips for companies such as Google. It also owns the software firm VMware.
co:broadcom.recent: The news about the company's own business was VMware's customers: a survey found licensing costs driving 90 percent of VMware users to explore options, and Topgolf said it saved over $11.3 million after leaving. None of that accounts for the fall in the share price.

co:spacex.standing: Builds reusable rockets, launches satellites and astronauts for governments and companies, and runs Starlink, a satellite internet network.
co:spacex.recent: SpaceX climbed 4% on a nationwide low-band spectrum deal for Starlink Mobile, a deal that sent Verizon and AT&T down 7%. Since then Ukraine has accused SpaceX of throttling the Starlink terminals its drones fly on, and the Starlink launch in India is still awaiting clearance. Musk blames that delay on Ambani's Reliance.

co:meta.standing: Owns Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp, used by more than three billion people, and earns nearly all its money from advertising on them.
co:meta.recent: Meta said its Muse model reached the AI frontier after 14 months of rebuilding, and the Muse agent topped the US App Store within two weeks. Its open-weights follow-up, Muse Spark Open, then scored 39, behind 4 Chinese rivals, and a Frankfurt court held Meta liable for scam ads impersonating Finanzfluss.

co:aramco.standing: Saudi Arabia’s state oil company, which pumps more oil than any other company. The government owns nearly all of it, and its dividends pay for much of the kingdom’s budget.
co:aramco.recent: Yemen's Houthis claimed a strike on an oil facility near Riyadh as tankers were hit in Hormuz, and a missile later set fire to an Aramco administrative building in Dhahran. Aramco's chief executive said almost 3 billion barrels of supply had been lost and restocking could take two years, and Saudi Arabia unexpectedly cut its oil prices to Asia.

co:tesla.standing: Makes electric cars, and the batteries that store power for homes and electricity grids. Led by Elon Musk, who also leads SpaceX.
co:tesla.recent: Tesla unveiled the 2026 Roadster, a sports car priced from at least $200,000, which Munster called an engineering flex with a SpaceX clue. A week earlier, Musk's push into India ended in acrimony, with Tesla's entry and Starlink both stalled there.

co:samsung.standing: One of the three companies that make most of the world’s memory chips, and one of the largest makers of smartphones and televisions.
co:samsung.recent: Samsung forecast a record quarterly operating profit of 107.4 trillion won, a 780% jump driven by the AI boom and a first for any tech company. Five days later Samsung and SK Hynix led a selloff that dragged South Korea's benchmark index down 5.5%, on doubts over AI spending and the rise of Chinese memory rivals.

co:micron.standing: The one large American maker of memory chips, the kind that hold data in phones, computers and AI data centres. Its two main rivals are Samsung and SK Hynix.

co:amd.standing: Designs processors for computers and data centres, where it competes with Intel, and AI chips, where it competes with Nvidia. Like Nvidia, it has TSMC make them.

co:berkshire.standing: A holding company built by Warren Buffett. It owns insurers, a railway and energy utilities outright, and holds large stakes in companies such as Apple and Coca-Cola.

co:lilly.standing: An American drugmaker. Its diabetes and weight-loss medicines, sold as Mounjaro and Zepbound, account for much of its growth.
co:lilly.recent: The fortnight's news about Eli Lilly was about its pipeline: a cousin of its obesity drugs is now in trials against alcohol use disorder, part of a push to test GLP-1 drugs on addiction, depression and schizophrenia. None of it accounts for the share price's moves.

co:jpmorgan.standing: The largest bank in the United States by assets, serving households, companies and governments.
co:jpmorgan.recent: The share's weakest stretch came as Fed officials questioned JPMorgan, Wells Fargo, Barclays and Morgan Stanley in a review spurred by private-credit worries: how much the banks have lent to the non-bank funds that now make loans banks once made, and what that exposure is worth if those loans sour.

co:skhynix.standing: A South Korean maker of memory chips, and the main supplier of the high-speed memory that Nvidia’s AI chips need.
co:skhynix.recent: On 13 October, a sell-off in Korean chip stocks, driven by doubts over AI spending and the rise of Chinese memory rivals, had Samsung and SK Hynix dragging South Korea's benchmark stock index down 5.5%.

co:walmart.standing: The world’s largest retailer by sales, with thousands of stores in the United States and abroad.
co:walmart.recent: The fortnight's news about Walmart itself was a change to its benefits: it said it would cover more than 250 medications, GLP-1s and insulin among them, at no cost for workers. Nothing in that explains the share price.

co:asml.standing: A Dutch company, and the only maker of the machines needed to print the most advanced chips. Every leading chipmaker buys from it, and its sales to China are restricted.
co:asml.recent: China's share of ASML's sales jumped from 14% to 23%, and its equipment sales there rose 109% even as the US pushed for tighter export curbs. Nothing reported in the fortnight accounts for the fall in the share price.

us-2y.standing: The interest rate the US government pays to borrow for two years. Of all Treasury yields it follows the Federal Reserve's policy rate most closely, so it shows where traders are betting that rate goes next.
us-2y.recent: A Reuters piece on 2026-10-05 asked what Washington would do if US bond yields kept rising, but nothing in the input names the policy decision or data release behind the climb.

us-mortgage.standing: The average interest rate US lenders charge on a 30-year fixed home loan, the mortgage most American buyers take. It follows long-dated Treasury yields, and it sets what a house costs each month and whether owners can afford to move.

ez-cpi.standing: The annual rise in consumer prices across the countries that share the euro, measured by Eurostat on one harmonised basket. The European Central Bank aims for 2% and sets the bloc's interest rates against it.

bnb.standing: The native token of BNB Chain, the blockchain network built by the exchange Binance. Holders use it to pay transaction fees on the chain and get trading discounts on Binance, so its price follows the exchange's fortunes and its regulators.

trx.standing: The token of the Tron blockchain, a network built for cheap, fast transfers. Most of its traffic is the dollar stablecoin Tether, so its price follows demand for moving dollars outside banks, especially in emerging markets.

sol.standing: The token of the Solana blockchain, used to pay its transaction fees and staked by the validators that secure it. Its price is a bet on how much trading and payment traffic the network wins, and it swings harder than Bitcoin.
sol.recent: Solana's news was about the network, not the token: the Solana Foundation launched DvP to settle institutional trades in seconds, a change to halve block times neared, and Oct. 21 was set for Alpenglow, an upgrade targeting 150-millisecond finality. None of it accounts for the price.

xrp.standing: The native token of the XRP Ledger, a payments network built for fast cross-border transfers. Ripple, the company most closely tied to it, holds a large share of the supply, so its legal and commercial fortunes move the price.
xrp.recent: The latest slide came as nearly $1 billion in leveraged crypto bets were liquidated across bitcoin, ether and XRP. Days earlier, the XRP Ledger Foundation explained a bug that had threatened the 100 billion XRP cap and sat hidden for years, while the ledger added controls for banks, stablecoins and tokenized funds.

hype.standing: The token of Hyperliquid, a blockchain built to run a derivatives exchange where traders bet on crypto prices with leverage. Trading fees fund buybacks of the token, so its price follows how much business the exchange does.
hype.recent: The one story about the venue in the fortnight was Bloomberg Business on Jeff Yan's plan to bring the entire financial industry onto Hyperliquid. It came weeks after the price peaked and does not account for the move.

doge.standing: A cryptocurrency launched as a joke around a Shiba Inu dog meme, with no cap on how many coins can exist. It has little use beyond payments and tipping, so its price moves on online attention and celebrity endorsement.

zec.standing: A cryptocurrency built on Bitcoin's design, with the same 21 million coin cap, that lets users hide sender, receiver and amount using zero-knowledge proofs. It is the main market price put on financial privacy on a public blockchain.
zec.recent: Zcash's 25-second blocks went live on a public testnet ahead of schedule, and the case for privacy coins in the age of AI got a fresh airing. Nearly $1 billion in crypto bets were then liquidated as bitcoin, ether and XRP slid. None of it accounts for the late-September run in the price.

boe-rate.standing: Bank Rate, the interest the Bank of England pays commercial banks on their reserves, set by its nine-member Monetary Policy Committee. British mortgage, savings and business loan rates are priced off it, and sterling moves with it.
boe-rate.recent: The one relevant report this fortnight was a split among Bank of England officials over the inflation risk facing the UK. It describes the argument over the next decision, not the cuts already made.

link.standing: The token of Chainlink, a network of oracles that feeds outside data such as prices into blockchain smart contracts. Node operators are paid in it, and much of decentralised lending relies on its price feeds.

boj-rate.standing: The Bank of Japan's short-term policy rate, the price of overnight money in yen. Kept near zero for decades, it made the yen the world's cheapest currency to borrow, so a rise pulls money back to Japan from markets everywhere.
boj-rate.recent: Yen-priced imports cost 24.5% more than a year ago, and wholesale inflation stayed elevated enough to keep another hike in view. Three sources said the Bank of Japan may declare its 2% goal reached, and Ueda said he can't tolerate underlying inflation further over it as hedge funds rebuilt short bets against the yen.

tcmb-rate.standing: The one-week repo rate at which the Central Bank of the Republic of Türkiye lends to commercial banks, and the country's main policy rate. It sets the cost of lira credit and shapes how attractive the currency is to hold against inflation.

pboc-rate.standing: The one-year loan prime rate, the benchmark the People's Bank of China steers and that banks use to price most new business and household loans. It sets the cost of credit across the world's second-largest economy.
pboc-rate.recent: This fortnight's news about the People's Bank of China concerned its reserves and its currency, not its rates. It bought 23 tonnes of gold in September and backed its yuan policy as the EU pressed over a 360.6 billion euros deficit, and none of that touches this rate.

bcb-rate.standing: The Selic, the overnight rate the Central Bank of Brazil sets to steer inflation toward its target. It prices government debt and bank lending across Latin America's largest economy, and the real's appeal to foreign money rises and falls with it.

bi-rate.standing: The rate Bank Indonesia sets for seven-day lending to commercial banks, its main policy tool. It steers borrowing costs across Southeast Asia's largest economy and is used to defend the rupiah when capital flows out.

cbr-rate.standing: The Bank of Russia's key rate, the price at which it lends to and takes deposits from commercial banks for a week. Rouble mortgages, company loans and the government's own borrowing costs are all priced off it.
cbr-rate.recent: The fortnight's news about the Bank of Russia was about other things: international reserves fell 4.85% in September to $731.76 bln, and the bank made no yuan purchases or sales for October 2 settlements. None of it bears on the key rate.

stocks:LLY.standing: An Indianapolis drugmaker whose tirzepatide, sold as Mounjaro for diabetes and Zepbound for obesity, made it the world's most valuable pharmaceutical company. Its share moves on demand, pricing and supply of that one drug class.
stocks:LLY.recent: Eli Lilly is now trialling a cousin of its obesity drug against alcohol use disorder, part of a wider push to redesign GLP-1 medicines for addiction, depression and schizophrenia. Nothing reported in the fortnight, including Walmart's move to cover some GLP-1s for its workers at no cost, accounts for the share price.

stocks:LMT.standing: The world's largest defence contractor by revenue and the maker of the F-35 fighter. Most of its sales come from the US government, so its share moves on Pentagon budgets and on foreign arms orders.
stocks:LMT.recent: Lockheed's own news in the fortnight was a product date, not an order: it said its PAC-3 Edge interceptor deploys from 2031. Separately, India's IAF Chief said the US had made no official offer to sell India F-35 jets. Neither accounts for the slide in the share.

mkt:set.standing: A capitalisation-weighted index of every common stock on the Stock Exchange of Thailand in Bangkok, the country's main market. It is sensitive to tourism flows and regional energy prices.

mkt:tadawul.standing: The Tadawul All Share Index covers every company on the Saudi Exchange's main market in Riyadh, the Arab world's largest by value and dominated by Aramco. It trades Sunday to Thursday, opening the global week before Tokyo.
mkt:tadawul.recent: Houthi missiles carried the Yemen war into the kingdom's economic core. A strike on Riyadh airport killed 13 and grounded 82% of Monday's flights, and a missile set fire to an Aramco building in Dhahran. The coalition also intercepted fire over Yanbu, the Red Sea terminal that carries crude around a closed Hormuz.

mkt:dfm.standing: The main index of the Dubai Financial Market, the stock exchange in Dubai, United Arab Emirates. It is the Gulf's main listing venue for property and banking, and trades Monday to Friday, unlike Riyadh.
mkt:dfm.recent: The UAE's non-oil output shrank 1.1% in the second quarter, the economy's contraction tied to the Hormuz war. Dubai fuel costs rose 37.52% in a year, and Iran rejected Washington's reply on reopening Hormuz. None of it is shown moving Dubai's listed property and banking shares.

mkt:pse.standing: The PSEi tracks 30 large companies listed on the Philippine Stock Exchange in Manila, the country's only bourse. It is a small, domestically driven market, and remittance flows from Filipinos working abroad move the index.
mkt:pse.recent: News out of Manila this fortnight carried a September survey finding 22.6% of Filipino families went involuntarily hungry, a warning of a stickier inflation wave, and China's ambassador cautioning against a cycle of retaliation. None of it accounts for the index's fall.

stocks:META.standing: The owner of Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp, which earns nearly all its revenue selling ads to reach more than three billion daily users. Its spending on AI data centres is among the heaviest in the industry.
stocks:META.recent: Meta launched Muse, claiming frontier AI after 14 months of rebuilding. Its agent topped the US App Store, and Muse Spark Open scored behind 4 Chinese rivals. A Frankfurt court held Meta liable for scam ads, and Brazil prosecutors probed its blocking of pro-Lula posts. None of it accounts for the share price.

stocks:GOOGL.standing: The parent company of Google, YouTube, Android and the Waymo robotaxi business. Most of its money comes from search advertising, so its share is a reading on the ad market and on whether AI erodes or extends search.
stocks:GOOGL.recent: A judge dismissed the antitrust suits Chegg and Penske brought against Google, and Google became the buyer for 890 megawatts of new nuclear output. Its Gemini 4 Argon model went only to trusted cyber defenders, and its own benchmarks put Claude 9 points ahead of it. None of this lines up with the share's swings.

stocks:MSFT.standing: The world's largest software company, maker of Windows, Office and the Azure cloud, and OpenAI's biggest backer. Its share is among the heaviest weights in US indices, so index funds worldwide move with it.
stocks:MSFT.recent: Washington suspended Microsoft from US green-card sponsorship amid fraud claims that also caught Adobe, and the shares fell 7.5%. The climb back came as Microsoft said it would roll out its own Maia AI chips across Azure by the gigawatt, compute it designs rather than buys.

stocks:DIS.standing: The share price of the entertainment group behind the Disney, Pixar and Marvel studios, the theme parks, Disney+, ABC and ESPN. The parks earn most of its profit, so it trades on household travel spending as much as on streaming.
stocks:DIS.recent: The one development in the input about Disney's own business is a report that Epic Games will let AI write all the code for its Disney shooter game, and nothing in it accounts for the share price.

poly-will-pedro-sanchez-be-the-next-prim.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Pedro Sánchez, Spain's Socialist prime minister, heads the government formed after the next general election. The price is what traders pay for a yes, and it moves on polls, coalition arithmetic and court cases.

poly-will-there-be-no-change-in-fed-inte.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the Federal Reserve leaves its policy rate unchanged at one scheduled meeting. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it moves on jobs data, inflation prints and officials' speeches.
poly-will-there-be-no-change-in-fed-inte.recent: Bets on a hold built as Warsh declined to steer markets: in Bangkok he called AI a shock to the economy and gave no guidance on the next move, and the missing words were read as a pause. That ran against a Fed where most officials still expect another rate hike by year-end, with inflation above target for 5.5 years.

poly-nato-x-russia-military-clash-by-oct.standing: A contract that pays out if Russian and NATO forces clash directly before its deadline. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it moves with incidents on the alliance's border and with Ukraine talks.
poly-nato-x-russia-military-clash-by-oct.recent: Washington spent the month easing off Moscow rather than confronting it: the US lifted oil sanctions on Russia, agreed to buy its diesel, threatened to halt the Europe-funded PURL arms pipeline to Ukraine and pushed an energy truce. The strikes reported stayed inside Ukraine and Russia.

stocks:0700.HK.standing: The Shenzhen company behind WeChat, the app most of China uses to message and pay, and the world's largest video-game publisher by revenue. Its Hong Kong share is one of the heaviest weights in the Hang Seng index.
stocks:0700.HK.recent: The one story about Tencent's own business was the retirement of its QClaw desktop agent, which shuts on 24 December. That came after the slide had already turned, and nothing in the input accounts for the share price.

stocks:BABA.standing: China's largest e-commerce company, owner of the Taobao and Tmall marketplaces and of the country's biggest cloud business. Its New York-listed share is the one most foreign investors use to take a view on Chinese consumers and tech.
stocks:BABA.recent: The trough came as Alibaba sued the Pentagon over its classification as a company tied to the Chinese military, a link the company denies outright. Since then it has launched N1 Pro glasses that verify payments by iris scan, and Apple's AI in China has been confirmed to run on Alibaba's Qwen models.

stocks:AMZN.standing: The world's largest online retailer and, through Amazon Web Services, the largest seller of rented computing power. The cloud arm earns most of the profit, so the share moves on data-centre demand more than on shopping.
stocks:AMZN.recent: Amazon's own news ran on several fronts: its Amazon Leo satellite line in Kirkland neared its first launch, Alexa's leadership was reshuffled after a high-end tablet release, and it was reported to be weighing $7 billion for the AI startup Decart, which Anthropic had walked away from. None of it is tied to a single turn in the share.

stocks:AIR.PA.standing: Europe's largest aerospace company and one of the two builders of large passenger jets, with defence, helicopter and space arms. Its share moves on how many aircraft it delivers against a backlog that runs years ahead.
stocks:AIR.PA.recent: The fortnight's news about Airbus was all on the defence side: its U740 Valkyrie drone flew at Mach 0.8, Spain picked the A321 for a new electronic intelligence aircraft, and it detailed progress on the Lakota Connector uncrewed cargo helicopter. None of it accounts for the fall in the share.

poly-will-flavio-bolsonaro-win-the-secon.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Flávio Bolsonaro wins Brazil's presidential election by a margin of four to eight percentage points. It prices how close the race is, not just who wins.
poly-will-flavio-bolsonaro-win-the-secon.recent: Brazil's presidential election went to a runoff after Bolsonaro's strong first-round showing left the left on the ropes, and this contract pays only on the size of his winning margin. Since then, researchers have logged over 1,000 Meta restrictions on political content in the campaign. None of it accounts for the swings in what traders will pay.

stocks:SPCX.standing: The rocket and satellite company founded by Elon Musk. It launches most of the world's orbital payloads on reusable Falcon rockets and runs Starlink, the satellite internet network that supplies most of its revenue.
stocks:SPCX.recent: SpaceX struck a nationwide low-band spectrum deal for Starlink Mobile, taking it onto the phone carriers' ground; Verizon and AT&T fell 7% on the news. In India, Starlink holds a licence but still cannot sell service, and Elon Musk turned his attack on Ambani over the delay.

stocks:1211.HK.standing: The Shenzhen carmaker that builds only battery-electric and plug-in hybrid vehicles and makes its own batteries. Its price cuts set the pace of China's car market, and its exports draw tariffs abroad.
stocks:1211.HK.recent: BYD said it will own 18 car-carrier ships by 2029, up from 8, because a shortage of vessels and war-driven freight costs, with Hormuz and Bab el-Mandeb disrupted, are holding back its exports. Nothing in the reporting accounts for the fall in the shares.

stocks:NOC.standing: A US defence contractor that builds the B-21 stealth bomber, the Sentinel nuclear missile, satellites and rocket motors. Most of its revenue comes from the US government, so its share follows the defence budget.
stocks:NOC.recent: Northrop's Talon Blue, a Collaborative Combat Aircraft, completed its first fully autonomous flight at Mojave on 3 October. Nothing else in the window was about the company's own business, and a first flight does not account for the fall in its share.

stocks:9984.T.standing: A Tokyo-listed holding company run by founder Masayoshi Son that owns most of chip designer Arm and backs technology firms through its Vision Funds. Its share moves with what investors will pay for AI.

stocks:005930.KS.standing: South Korea's largest company and the world's biggest maker of memory chips, alongside phones and displays. It is the heaviest weight in Seoul's benchmark index, so its share moves the whole market.
stocks:005930.KS.recent: Samsung forecast a 780% jump in quarterly operating profit, to 107.4 trillion won, on the AI boom, and the share fell anyway. The heaviest day came when Samsung and SK Hynix dragged South Korea's benchmark down 5.5% in a chip selloff over AI spending and Chinese memory rivals.

stocks:000660.KS.standing: South Korea's second-largest chipmaker, making the DRAM and NAND memory inside servers, phones and PCs. It is a leading supplier of the high-bandwidth memory stacked beside AI processors, so its share follows data-centre spending.
stocks:000660.KS.recent: On 13 October SK Hynix and Samsung led a chip sell-off in Seoul that dragged South Korea's benchmark stock index down 5.5%, over doubts about AI spending and the rise of Chinese memory rivals that compete with the core of its business.

stocks:BHP.standing: An Australian miner, one of the world's largest, based in Melbourne. It digs iron ore in Western Australia and copper in Chile, so its share moves with Chinese steel demand and the copper price.

poly-2026-balance-of-power-d-senate-d-ho.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Democrats win both the Senate and the House in the 2026 US midterms. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, which would give one party control of legislation and confirmations.

poly-will-the-democratic-party-control-t.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Democrats win a majority of the US House of Representatives in the midterms. The price is what traders pay for that outcome; the House majority controls spending bills and investigations.
poly-will-the-democratic-party-control-t.recent: No US House race surfaced in the fortnight's news. The nearest item, 39 states and 145 tribal nations urging the Supreme Court to review prediction markets, concerns whether contracts like this one are legal, not who wins.

stocks:7974.T.standing: The Kyoto company that makes the Switch consoles and the Mario and Zelda games that sell them. It earns from its own hardware and its own software together, so its profits rise and fall with each console's life cycle.

stocks:UBI.PA.standing: The French publisher behind Assassin's Creed, Far Cry and Rainbow Six, listed in Paris. Its fortunes ride on a few big releases a year, so a delay or a weak launch moves the share more than the wider games market does.

wiki-openai.standing: How many people read the English Wikipedia article on OpenAI each day, the San Francisco lab behind ChatGPT. It jumps when the company ships a model, loses a senior figure or lands in a dispute.
wiki-openai.recent: OpenAI released more than 350 mathematical findings in one day, after researchers in Cambridge rushed a 95-page paper out ahead of one of its proofs. Then the FBI arrested an engineer over a recording device hidden in a meeting room, and the FTC sent civil investigative demands asking whether its security incidents harmed Americans.

stocks:BAC.standing: The second-largest US bank by assets, listed on the New York Stock Exchange. Its share price tracks US interest rates, consumer credit and deposit flows across tens of millions of American accounts.
stocks:BAC.recent: The US Treasury imposed more than $1.21bn in penalties on Bank of America for anti-money-laundering and sanctions violations, the third-largest in the department's history, after the bank reported $5 billion in suspicious transactions late. The fine landed the day after the last reading, so it does not explain the slide before it.

stocks:SHEL.standing: One of the world's largest oil and gas companies, headquartered in London, and the biggest trader of liquefied natural gas. Its shares move with crude and gas prices and with the cash it returns to shareholders.
stocks:SHEL.recent: The one development about Shell's own business came after the latest close: it agreed to sell its Nigerian domestic gas business, which serves more than 130 customers, to Vaaris Energy. Nothing else in the fortnight concerned the company, so none of it accounts for the climb.

stocks:2222.SR.standing: Saudi Arabia's state oil company, the world's largest crude producer, listed on the Saudi Exchange in Riyadh since 2019. The state keeps almost all of it, so the small float trades on oil prices and the dividend.
stocks:2222.SR.recent: The Houthis claimed a strike on an oil facility near Riyadh, a missile set fire to an Aramco administrative building in Dhahran, and Aramco's CEO said replenishing crude and fuel supplies could take two years after almost 3 billion barrels were lost. Saudi Arabia also cut its oil prices to Asia. None of it accounts for the share's path.
